data.long_meaning: The name Hanu is derived from Sanskrit, where it means 'jaw' or 'mouth'. In Hindu mythology, Hanuman, a powerful monkey god, is named after this term as he is known to have an unbreakable jaw and an eloquent mouth. He is considered a symbol of strength, devotion, and wisdom. The name Hanu carries the meaning “Jaw, mouth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Hanu usually hope their child will grow to embody jaw, mouth and live with faith, good character and purpose.

He is revered for his extraordinary strength, loyalty, courage, and wisdom. Hanuman is also known as the embodiment of devotion (bhakti) and is invoked for protection, cure from illnesses and success in endeavors. Thus, the name Hanu carries a rich cultural legacy in India.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, Hanuman represents the transcendental power of devotion, courage, and steadfastness. His name inspires hope, faith, and steady determination in the face of challenges. Hanuman is believed to be an incarnation of Lord Shiva and Lord Vayu, and is the embodiment of the power of consciousness. His name connects us to the divine and instills a sense of inner strength and peace.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Hanu is derived from the Sanskrit word 'hastini', which means 'elephant'. In Hindu mythology, the elephant symbolizes strength, power, and wisdom. Therefore, the name Hanu signifies a strong, wise, and powerful individual.
